thread:
Erica Chen: Quick async check — Wave 6 dedicated capacity. Need a short status: procurement ETAs, reservation mapping to customer commits, and any blockers for next-week canary. TL;DR: we need a stable manifest by end of day tomorrow so runtime can pin canary nodes.

Michael O'Neill: Procurement update: vendor #3 confirmed a partial ship — 40x H100 arriving week of 2026-04-12, remaining 60 delayed ~2 weeks. Working with them on expedited routing. I'll push an interim manifest with the 40 confirmed units.

Sudhir Rao: Thanks. Two quick asks: (1) Which reservations do we map those 40 GPUs to? we had priority customers A/B/C — need explicit mapping so billing & capacity tools don't double-book. (2) Fallback policy: if the remaining 60 slip past +2 weeks, are we auto-falling back to smaller instance types or routing to hosted?

Alex Kim: Cluster readiness notes: Rack power test slot is 2026-04-10 03:00-05:00 UTC for the first 4 cabinets. Firmware window for NICs is 2026-04-11 22:00-23:30 UTC (non-disruptive but needs ops approval). Cable kits still pending from procurement (ETA 2 days after the first ship). If cable kits delayed, we can light up partial racks but not full SKU density.

Michael O'Neill: @Sudhir mapping plan: I'll allocate the 40 units as: 20 -> Priority A (reserved), 10 -> Priority B (soft-reserve, will be promoted if tests pass), 10 -> canary pool (runtime). I'll create a PR to the reservation manifest: branch `wave6-manifest-interim`.

Erica Chen: Sounds good. @Michael please include `reservation_id` fields and expected serial ranges so billing can reconcile. Also document the fallback routing policy: prefer smaller pinned VMs in eu-west if GPU shortfall > 30%.

Deploy Bot: reservation created: resv-20260412-wave6-partial (40 units) — status: provisional — approver required.

Nina Patel: Quick note from compliance: PDNS updates required for any public-facing canary endpoints. If canary uses customer data, we need the data flow signoff before routing production traffic. Who's owning that?

Sudhir Rao: I'll own the fallback policy doc and add the decision table for routing (model variants + cost delta + latency budget). Will sketch a small table and post as a gist.

Michael O'Neill: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/capacity-manifests/pull/482 — includes mapping + serial ranges + a note about delayed 60 units. @Sudhir can you review? tagging @Alex for cluster notes.

Alex Kim: Reviewed cluster notes in the PR — left one nit about rack labeling (use `rack-zone` tag). If cable kits show up late, we should sequence canary on cabinets 1/3/5 to keep thermal balancing.

Erica Chen: OK — owners: @Michael manifest PR + procurement comms, @Sudhir fallback policy doc, @Alex rack sequencing & power test owner, @Nina PDNS/data-flow signoff. Please update the PR/Docs by EOD tomorrow. If anyone can't hit that, call it out here.

Michael O'Neill: I can hit EOD tomorrow. Will queue an ops alert once the interim manifest lands. :thumbsup:

Nina Patel: I'll start the PDNS checklist and loop in security for the data-flow review — aiming for reminder ping on 2026-04-11.

Sudhir Rao: Drafting fallback doc now, will link by EOD today.

Erica Chen: Great. One last ask — add a short rollback/fail-open play for canary: if model latency > 2x baseline, auto-shift canary to hosted variant and mark the cluster for manual triage. Keep it simple.

Michael O'Neill: Adding rollback snippet to PR:```\nfallback_policy:\n  threshold_latency_ms: 200\n  action: shift_to_hosted_variant\n  notify: #eng-sre\n```\n
Erica Chen: Perfect. Thanks all — closing this thread after PR + docs updated.
